claim: The music path's log-mean-exp is not length-normalised in practice. On the synthetic stress, music FPR goes from .200 to .398 (DB heads) and from .185 to .420 (S3 MERT-6+12 heads). claim: The synthetic protocol is an approximation. Constituent files come from distinct groups, so windows are more independent than in one long recording, which overstates both max inflation for reals and evidence gain for fakes. In the FILE-level synthetic, presence is taken as the max over constituents.

claim: The shipped-configuration DF-Arena voice heads (all rows of cache_v4, DB protocol) are formally cap-bound: all 3 seeds pick epoch 50. But lifting the cap to 150 epochs with patience 10 at lr 1e-4 gives val ens EER 0.0510 -> 0.0500 and held-out 0.1101 -> 0.1105 (no change). At lr 3e-4, val goes to 0.0476 and held-out to 0.1084, a -0.0018 change inside the seed sd of 0.0042. Under the P1 protocol only 1/3 seeds hit the cap, and the long schedule moves val 0.0502 -> 0.0486; P1 has no held-out estimate.
evidence: research/top15/work/r2/runs/fullvoice_db__{base,long,long_lr3e-4}.json and fullvoice_p1__{base,long}.json; table.md; report.json; logs/fullvoice_*.log (e.g. 'db base 41 best_epoch 50 hit_cap True'). full_voice.py reuses run.train, a copy of data_v4/train_backbone_heads.py::train.
counterevidence: Val EER moves in steps of about 0.0002 (about 1 file). The lexicographic (EER, BCE) key lets falling BCE reset patience, so 'cap hit' partly reflects BCE creep.
consequence: Do not spend effort on longer voice schedules. The epoch cap is not what limits the Linear voice head on held-out.

claim: On backbone rows (18,260 voice items, 72 updates/epoch) the base Linear heads stop before the cap (best epochs 26-46). More optimization still helps them modestly on held-out. DF-Arena goes 0.1195 -> 0.1138 (150/10) -> 0.1119 (lr 3e-4). AntiDeepfake goes 0.1408 -> 0.1369 (150/10) -> 0.1336 (lr 3e-4, or batch 64).
evidence: runs/voice_df__{base,long,long_lr3e-4}.json, runs/voice_ad__{base,long,long_lr3e-4,long_b64,long_b1024}.json; report.json test section; choice_lock.json val table

consequence: The S3 screen heads (ads_compare) were trained with fewer updates than the full-data heads, so they were mildly under-optimized. Any backbone-row screen should use lr 3e-4 or more updates.

claim:
A 2-layer MLP voice head beats the Linear head by a large margin on held-out. The variants were chosen by the pre-declared val rule before any held-out EER was seen.
- DF-Arena fc5 inputs, standardized, Linear(1280,256)-GELU-Linear(256,2): 0.1195 -> 0.0901 on backbone rows (seed sd 0.0039). The post-lock confirmation on all rows gave 0.1101 -> 0.0815.
- AntiDeepfake embeddings with the ResMLP (pretrained proj_fc Linear plus a zero-init 2-layer branch): 0.1408 -> 0.1171 (sd 0.0001). The plain MLP gave 0.1234.
evidence: runs/voice_df__mlp_long.json, voice_df__resmlp_long.json, voice_ad__resmlp_long.json, voice_ad__mlp_long.json, fullvoice_db__mlp_long.json; choice_lock.json written 2026-09-27 14:04:45 KST; PROTOCOL.md amendments with timestamps; logs/fullvoice_mlp_confirm.out

consequence: This is the largest head-level held-out gain measured so far, larger than the S3 backbone change. It is the best candidate for a next submission if the runtime is changed.

claim:
Official held-out ADS in the exact ads_compare pipeline (presence heads, FILE ensemble refit on val, voice CDF fusion 1:0.5):
- S3-like baseline: 0.87267.
- DF-Arena MLP only: 0.88161, +0.0089 (95% group CI 0.0053-0.0123).
- AntiDeepfake ResMLP only: 0.87438, +0.0017 (CI -0.0003 to 0.0045, P(<=0)=0.056).
- Both MLPs: 0.88643, +0.0138 (CI 0.0092-0.0174).
With both, FILE EER goes .0996 -> .0834 and VOICE EER .1106 -> .0823.

The MLP gain is spread across held-out sources rather than concentrated in one cell. With each model at its own EER threshold, DF Linear -> MLP:
- HAIM fake miss .409 -> .281
- constructed_enhanced real FP .242 -> .135
- constructed_mix real FP .207 -> .103
- FLEURS-ko real FP .114 -> .096
- MLAAD miss .044 -> .024
- constructed_mix fake miss .105 -> .126 (the only cell that got worse)
Length dependence of real scores is unchanged: within-source Spearman 0.241 -> 0.262.

claim: No MERT layer variant beats concat [6,12] under the val rule. The softmax-weighted 8-layer sum (sls8) is clearly worse: val ens .1330 vs .1119, held-out .1946 vs .1847. Its learned weights stay near uniform (0.11-0.16, highest on L9 at about 0.15). Concat of all 8 layers is unstable: val seed sd 0.011, and one seed stopped at epoch 5. [3,6,9] ties on val ens (.1119) and is mixed on held-out: ens .1778 vs .1847, but seed-mean .1843 vs .1810.
evidence: runs/music__{L6_12,L3_6_9,L3_6_9_12,concat8,sls8}.json; choice_lock.json layer_weights; report.json
counterevidence: SLS was a plain softmax sum with uniform init at lr 1e-3. Per-layer gating or a higher alpha lr was not tried.
consequence: Music is not a head-level lever with these features. Keep 6+12.

claim:
There is a latent runtime crash for any head that saturates.
- decision_heads.quantile_table adds i*1e-12 to the table, so a val max of exactly 1.0 gives a table top of 1+1e-9.
- component_fusion.fuse then returns a value above 1 through np.interp.
- full_bank_submission.py passes the fused VOICE score unclipped (line 136) to validate_predictions (line 167), which raises.
The MLP heads do saturate: 128 val and 58 held-out seed-mean scores equal 1.0. The runtime also hardcodes nn.Linear(1280,2) with strict loading for voice_* (line 34) and voice_ad_* heads.
evidence: ads.py first run failed with 'ValueError: Probability outside finite [0, 1] for v4_00b63c566db47b436c3b81a3/VOICE_FAKE_PROB'; decision_heads.py:78-81; full_bank_submission.py:34,72-73,136,167; saturation count from runs/voice_df__mlp_long.json
consequence: Deploying an MLP head needs a clip (min(1, fuse(...))) and new head-loading code. Without them the submission raises a runtime error and burns a slot. Current S3 Linear heads peak at 0.999997, so S3 is not affected.

claim:
Batch and compute:
- Loading: 20-40 s per group.
- Head training: 5-38 s per seed on 4 CPU threads; a whole 3-seed run takes 49-117 s wall. Peak RSS is 0.9-1.5 GB (voice) and up to 3.6 GB (8-layer music).
- Updates/epoch at 256 files/update: 72 (voice, backbone rows), 97 (voice, full), 117 (P1), 28 (music).
- On AntiDeepfake Linear 150/10: batch 1024 (18 updates/epoch) gives val .0482 / held-out .1432; batch 256 gives .0482/.1369; batch 64 gives .0443/.1336; lr 3e-4 at batch 256 gives .0432/.1336.
evidence: /usr/bin/time -l in logs/*.log; seed train_seconds and updates_per_epoch in runs/*.json; table.md
counterevidence: Timings were taken with up to 3 parallel runs plus other lanes' load.
consequence: A larger batch at fixed lr and epochs means fewer updates and worse results. Cloud GPU time for heads is worthless; a GPU matters only for backbone feature extraction.

claim: The voice route is limited by the capacity of its Linear head, not only by the representation. A train-only MLP on the same DF-Arena fc5 inputs reaches held-out 0.0815. That is below the 0.100 voice test EER that the P1 Linear heads give even after training on the test rows.
evidence: R2-F3 numbers; lane2 finding (P1 heads in-sample voice test EER 0.10039, _workspace/fusion_20260927/p1_all_w1/fusion_report.json)
counterevidence: The two numbers come from different row sets (5,139 vs 6,450 held-out rows) and different protocols.
consequence: This revises lane2's 'representation-limited' hypothesis. Head architecture is a real lever for the voice route, and the frozen features carry more separable information than a linear readout extracts.

claim: A P1-refit package with the MLP voice heads, fusion clip and new head loading would improve the LB by about +0.004 to +0.009 ADS (about +0.004 to +0.008 total).
evidence: R2-F4 held-out delta x lane2 held-out-to-LB ratio (0.63, one pair) and val-to-LB ratios (0.32-0.39)
counterevidence: Head-only LB moves so far were at most ±0.002 ADS. The LB distribution (phone channel, 4-60 s) differs from held-out.
consequence: Worth one submission slot as the best head-level candidate, after a CPU parity run and ideally an L4 runtime check. It cannot by itself reach the top-15 cut (+0.08 total).

evidence: ads.py output 'max |R2 base - ads_compare| per component'; runs/fullvoice_p1__base.json vs _workspace/p1_refit_cpu/results.json; runs/fullvoice_db__base.json vs _keep_best_20260926/train_duration_balanced/results.json

consequence: The variant deltas are attributable to the changed knob, not to reimplementation drift.

claim: Song-aware VOICE: add the file's own music-head CDF to VOICE fusion when music is present (ours 1, AD 1, music 0.5*Pm, soft gate, chosen on val; FILE rules keep the S3 Fv). Held-out official ADS rises 0.87267 -> 0.87731 (+0.0046); voice EER 0.1106 -> 0.0875; FILE and music unchanged.

This replicates _workspace/audit_20260927/ads_compare.py evaluate(): the S3 config reproduces test ADS 0.87267 exactly. Oracle-gated voice gain +0.0245, group-bootstrap CI [0.0128, 0.0390] over 2,112 groups (cross_component_check.out.txt).

The reverse direction (voice evidence into MUSIC) hurts: -0.0056, CI [-0.013, +0.003].

claim: The discordant voice/music share of the official test decides the LB sign of R3-F1, and it is unknown.
evidence: Held-out music-context voice rows are about 26% discordant (constructed_mix 235, constructed_song 65; cross_component_check.out.txt). DACON scores VOICE and MUSIC separately, which suggests mixes exist, but no composition is published (brief).
consequence: Treat R3-F1 as a one-slot bet on top of a validated base (S3 if its L4 run succeeded, otherwise P1 with members ours+music). Do not tune it from the LB.

claim: Music EER is limited by the representation: file-mean MERT with logistic regression (val-selected layers [3,6,9,12]) gives held-out music EER 0.1884, vs 0.1847 for WindowMIL MERT-6+12 on the same 2,149 rows. All layer subsets fall between 0.184 and 0.20.

counterevidence: This used a simplified class-balanced weighting, not the full class x source x generator weights.
consequence: More head, pooling or layer tweaks on MERT will not move music (weight 0.3). A music gain needs a new representation: a second frozen encoder, or fine-tuning.

claim: The Afchar et al. Fourier-peak AI-music fingerprint is unsuitable here. It separates Lyria-3-Pro when trained and tested on the same generator (CV AUC 0.992 vs FMA, 1.000 vs SonicMaster). Leave-one-generator-out against an unseen real source (HAIM B1 SonicMaster, REAL under DACON rules), AUC falls to 0.01-0.66 (Lyria 0.579).
evidence: research/top15/work/r3/fourier_peak_check.py and fourier_logo_check.py (.out.txt) on local audio at 16 kHz. Paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.19108 (unseen Udio-32 39.8%). Hard negatives: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14916
counterevidence: Small local sets (e.g. udio 24, elevenlabs 24); against same-source reals, transfer is 0.71-0.93.
consequence: Drop spectral-artifact detectors. DACON counts AI-mastered or enhanced real audio as REAL, and that audio carries similar artifacts.

claim: Both trained voice heads (DB protocol) still over-flag narrowband phone audio and singing contexts. Real FPR at the EER threshold: tel_opus8 0.300 (DF) / 0.412 (AD) vs 0.05-0.18 for other codecs; musan_music 0.33/0.43. Held-out voice EER in music context is 0.21-0.22 vs 0.035-0.048 in speech context.
evidence: research/top15/work/r3/codec_heads_check.out.txt; routed_fusion_check.out.txt (speech-ctx/music-ctx split)
counterevidence: tel_opus8 n=80 with group structure not bootstrapped; which phone codecs the official test uses is UNVERIFIED.
consequence: These are the cells that codec/telephony augmentation and fine-tuning address in the literature (AT-ADD T1 top systems; SVDD 2024). Frozen-feature heads cannot fix them.

claim: Zero-shot AntiDeepfake-1B scores DACON-REAL enhanced speech as more fake than its parent speech (AUC 0.748; 23.3% vs 3.8% above 0.5). It also flags 68% of singing/music-context real voice. This fits the AntiDeepfake post-training data, which puts restored speech (FLEURS-R, LibriTTS-R) in the 'speech with artifacts' pool.
evidence: research/top15/work/r3/ad_restored_check.out.txt (members_all.csv, val+test); https://arxiv.org/html/2506.21090 Table I and Section III-A (restored-speech category)
counterevidence: The paper text does not give an explicit per-file label table. After training, the AD head is better than DF on enhanced reals (FPR 0.158 vs 0.242).
consequence: AD needs trained heads, or fine-tuning with DACON's label convention; zero-shot use is ruled out. Record this label-convention mismatch in the round-2 model report. The checkpoint license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (https://github.com/nii-yamagishilab/AntiDeepfake).

claim: Type-aware routing of the AD fusion weight (AT-ADD-style) picked on val (speech-context w=1, music-context w=4) worsens held-out voice EER: 0.1171 vs 0.1106 for the global 0.5 weight (delta -0.0069, CI [-0.016, +0.002]).
evidence: research/top15/work/r3/routed_fusion_check.py/.out.txt; routing idea from https://arxiv.org/html/2608.14249v1 (T2 #1/#3)
counterevidence: Routing used the oracle MUSIC_PRESENT label (runtime presence AUC is about 0.999).
consequence: Val singing contexts do not represent held-out ones. Do not add routed or context-specific weights fitted on val.

claim: Changing voice window pooling at inference, the AT-ADD median/multi-crop idea, gives little. Val-selected top-2 cuts held-out voice EER 0.1107 -> 0.1060 (CI of gain [-0.0009, 0.0104]). Median removes the length correlation (rho 0.24 -> 0.01) but raises EER to 0.1403 (0.283 on files of 15 s or longer).
evidence: research/top15/work/r3/window_pool_check.py/.out.txt (DurationBalanced DF-Arena heads, cache_v4 fp32); median pooling source: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.14249v1 (T1 #3)
counterevidence: Heads were trained with max-MIL, so training with the new pooling might do better (untested).
consequence: The length correlation is partly real evidence, not only bias. At most about +0.001 ADS; not worth a slot alone.

claim: SLS, AASIST and Nes2Net back-ends need frame-level SSL sequences (B x D x T), but our caches hold only pooled window vectors. DF-Arena already implements SLS-style per-layer attentive pooling with sigmoid layer gates, a weighted sum and a 4-block conformer.

consequence: These back-ends need re-extraction of frame sequences on GPU, which does not fit the budget. Drop them for this round.

claim: Literature consensus (2024-2026) puts the large gains in fine-tuning or partial fine-tuning of SSL front ends with codec/channel/RawBoost augmentation, plus multi-encoder score fusion. Frozen or prompt-tuned encoders trail full fine-tuning.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.23437 (frozen WPT 73.35 vs FT 76.73 F1); https://arxiv.org/html/2608.14249v1 (all top systems use augmentation and ensembles; T1 #3 partial FT of the last 6 XLSR-1B layers); https://arxiv.org/html/2506.21090 (FT 1B 11.86% vs 19.96% without post-training at 4 s); https://arxiv.org/html/2504.06753 (frozen 32.58 vs FT 27.68 avg EER); https://arxiv.org/html/2509.12003 (4-encoder fusion better out of domain)
counterevidence: In-repo EAT full-FT (09-16, n=40 per subset): seen-music EER 0.10 vs 0.217 frozen MERT, but OOD 0.30 vs 0.20. Fine-tuning on small data can hurt OOD (_workspace/fullft8_live/h100x1_fullft8_run/*/evaluation.json).
consequence: A step change in ADS most plausibly needs GPU work on audio (voice stems). With $9.85 of VESSL credit (about 3.3 H100-h) and 44 h left, only a bounded extraction fits; fine-tuning does not.

claim: No public DACON 236749 solution beyond the baseline exists. Codeshare holds only the official baseline; the public GitHub repos are baseline derivatives (PANNs+HTDemucs+DF-Arena, max/soft-or fusion) with no reported score.
evidence: /tmp/dacon_codeshare.json (total_list has 1 item, cs_id 14153); https://github.com/kimdong20020619-ctrl/Deep-voice ; https://github.com/sideotod/deepvoice-detection (fetched 2026-09-27); https://github.com/hyunI0326/dacon_voice returned 404
consequence: Nothing to borrow. Top teams' methods are unknown.

claim: Recommendation E2: add a second frozen audio/music encoder (EAT-large, MIT license; or MuQ, CC-BY-NC) and fuse its CDF score into MUSIC. This is the most promising GPU-bounded lever for music.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.14249v1 (T2 #1 and #2 both use EAT-large for non-speech); https://arxiv.org/html/2606.16612 (frozen MuQ+MERT+Fx-Encoder++ MoE, +18.5 F1 on the newest generators); https://arxiv.org/html/2509.12003 (score fusion of frozen encoders); R3-F3 (MERT representation-limited); licenses from https://github.com/cwx-worst-one/EAT and https://huggingface.co/OpenMuQ/MuQ-large-msd-iter
counterevidence: The in-repo EAT full-FT was worse OOD (frozen use was not tested). Mixture-level features could couple fake vocals into MUSIC, as R3-F1 does in the opposite direction.
